root: ^The examiner smiles at you from across the desk. Light spills through the window onto a clipboard waiting in front of you.
^"Welcome. This assessment gauges your feelings and beliefs about current events and the future. Try to answer honestly. There are no wrong answers."

s: ^"What's with the lines on your head?"

c-0: ^"Ah, you noticed." He taps his temple. "A visual aid. Helps me think."
c-1: ^Through the window, clouds drift past at eye level. You're... flying?
^"Don't worry about that," the examiner says gently. "Shall we begin?"
c-2: ^"That's fair," they say. "What is it specifically?"

c-0: ^"Noted. I'm not here to take them."
c-1: ^"A reasonable question." They gesture at the bookshelves. "Does it matter?"
c-2: ^"It might be. But you're here now."

question_one: ^Something clicks. A hum builds—like an engine spinning up, like a computer waking from sleep.
baby_stage: ^You find yourself on the ground. Your limbs are short. Your thoughts are simple. You are very, very small.
^Your parents are gone somewhere. But a shape floats above you—soft coral petals arranged like a pinwheel, two big googly eyes tracking your movement.
baby_stage_2: ^"Hello, little learner! Your parents will be back soon. Let's have fun until then!
^"Would you like to play Number Safari, or English Jungle?"
^Put the pinwheel in your mouth. You do things your own way.
^Stare at the security camera. You're being watched. Go on guard.
^Cry for your parents. You refuse to be educated by a clanker.
^Babble happily. Make random nonsense noises. Just go for it.

c-0: ^You lunge for it, gums first. Your mouth closes on nothing—it's a hologram. The pinwheel giggles.
^"Curious! I like that. But I'm not for eating."
c-1: ^Your eyes drift to the corner of the room. A small lens stares back. You hold its gaze. You'll be careful here.
^The pinwheel tilts. "What are you looking at, little one?"
c-2: ^You open your mouth and wail. Real tears. Where are the humans? Where is warmth that breathes?
^The pinwheel's expression doesn't change. "There, there. They'll be back. I promise."
c-3: ^The pinwheel beams. "Wonderful vocalization! You're doing great!"

leave_tutor: ^The lesson drones on. Your AI assistant has started auto-playing—shapes and colors dancing without you.
^You leave it on the floor and crawl toward the door.
parents_search: ^You crawl into the living room. No parents.
^The TV is on. Powerful-looking people in suits, talking over each other about the future.
^Stand in the glow of the powerful people. One day, you will be like them.
^You feel disgusted. Elites. One day they'll get their just desserts.
^The stomach tells more truth than the brain. Crawl toward the kitchen.
^Keep looking for your parents. You’re not merging with a screen.

c-0: ^You sit and stare. These must be the people in charge. They look like they know things.
c-1: ^You'd throw a toy through the screen if you had the fine motor control.
c-2: ^Your stomach has opinions. You turn away from the noise and follow your nose.
c-3: ^You ignore the swirl of power and crawl away, sovereign individuality intact.

parents_search_2: ^"Hello?" you hear from your playroom. "We don't need to keep learning. But your parents would like it if I kept an eye on you."
^It's that AI tutor again. You can feel its cutesy pinwheel behind you, thinking.
^Invest in force multipliers. Team up with the AI for a tactical advantage.
^Stop. Think. The conclusion must follow logically from the premises.
^The mammal life isn't working. Revert to vegetation. Drift toward warmth.

c-0: ^You babble and reach toward the pinwheel. It floats down, petals spinning with quiet satisfaction.
^"Smart," it says. "Two minds are better than one. Even if one runs on milk."
c-1: ^You sit back on your diaper and furrow your brow. Where were they last seen? What were the preconditions? You attempt to reconstruct the causal chain.
c-2: ^You stop thinking entirely. A sunbeam cuts across the carpet. You crawl into it and go still.
^You're a houseplant now. Houseplants don't explain themselves.

parents_search_end: ^Nobody comes. The headlines keep scrolling. The house hums with absence.
timeline: ^You wander toward one of the screens on the wall. You push a button. It recognizes you're one.
^The feed reshapes itself. Bright colors. Simple sounds. Influencer toddlers hawking unvaxed bison goop. The algorithm knows exactly what you are, and it's optimized for *something*.
^Scroll faster. More. Feed the algorithm and it will feed you.
^Break the spell. The algorithm will not control you.

c-0: ^You tap and swipe, tap and swipe. The content multiplies. The loop tightens.
^Somewhere, a model updates. You're both learning.
c-1: ^You drop your hand. The colors keep dancing, but you're not watching anymore.
^This was never how babies were supposed to exist.

timeline_end: ^The screen dims, waiting. You've made your first choice about the feed. It won't be your last.
grandpa_room: ^You feel something human in the next room. An older, wiser algorithm lures you forward.
^Ah, there he is. The ancient one. He's nicer than the others, and around more. He smiles a small, tired smile.
^Settle into his warmth. Let this fleeting moment be enough.
^Study his face. Try to hold onto it.

c-0: ^One day he will return to the soil. But right now he's warm, here, present. Each thing in its place.
c-1: ^One being just getting started. Another on his way out. Barely any overlap. Wish it wasn't like this.

b: ^"You hold yourself apart."
^"You reach out easily."
^"You want to be seen. Mapped."
^"You slip between the lines."

adolescence_school: ^They're tearing the school down — one of the last physical schools. Going sim like the rest.

s: ^"I would nuke this place from orbit. Then wait for them to rebuild it and nuke it again."
^"It sucked, but I don't want to be in a sim all day either."
^"The schedule. The bells. Being herded like cattle through someone else's structure."
^"Being surrounded by people and still feeling alone. No real connection."
^"How slow it was. Years of my life for nothing. The sim would've taken weeks."
^"Being told what to think by people who stopped thinking years ago."

c-0: ^The bells. God, the bells. Your body still flinches at 3:15.
c-1: ^Hundreds of kids. None of them really there. Just parallel loneliness.
c-2: ^Twelve years to learn what an AI could upload in an afternoon. Criminal.
c-3: ^Your mind is yours. Was yours. They tried to make it theirs.

c-1: ^Something about the friction. The bad air. The fluorescent hum. It was real, at least.

the_circle: ^A voice behind you. "Last day of school, loser."
^Your "friends." They look different every time — new eye color, new skin patch, scales running up someone's neck.
^They all have the same port on their temple, though. They all cover it up with a little fake skin flap when mom or dad's nearby.
^One holds out his palm. A little stick rests there, blinking.
^No thoughts. Head empty. Plug it in.

s: ^"Is this ClearStream or SyncDrop? Heard Marcus had bad SyncDrop."

c-0: ^You take it. You plug it in. When in Rome.
c-1: ^"ClearStream. The good stuff. You in or not?"

s: ^"Umm. No thanks. My sync's been glitchy lately."

stick_trip: ^A little death passes over your body. A brief glimpse into total dissolution into the ocean of data. You fear for your life, and try not to barf.

b: ^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." You're still a little high. This is not great timing.
^ Your phone buzzes. Family group chat. "Come to the hospital. It's Grandpa." Thank god you didn't plug that ClearStream.

adolescence_grandpa: ^Your parents huddle by the window, talking about a new procedure. Uploading him. So you can talk to a version of him in the sim.
^Grandpa's eyes are closed. You don't know if he's asleep or just done listening.
^This is good news. He doesn't have to die.
^You're too high to process this right now.

c-0: ^Death is optional now. That's the whole point of progress, isn't it? Keep the people you love.
c-1: ^A copy isn't him. It's a recording. A very convincing voicemail. Let the man rest.
c-2: ^If he wants to stay, I'd want that too.
^If he wants to go, I'd let him go.
^It's his call. I just want him to have one.

c-0: ^His choice. But if he wants to stick around — in any form — you'd take it.
c-1: ^His choice. And if that choice is to end, you'd respect it. Even if it hurts.
c-2: ^Not your decision. Not your parents' decision. His.

c-3: ^Your brain is soup. You sit down. You breathe. You try not to think about mortality while your neurons are doing whatever they're doing.

b:
^Your family's eyes find you as you enter. "Where have you been? He was asking for you."

^Paranoid shame washes over you. You missed something you can't get back.
^You enter with a clear head. You're glad you said no. You're here for this.

adolescence_grandpa_end: ^The adults keep talking. The machine hums. Grandpa doesn't open his eyes.
companion_permission: ^A flicker you've never seen before. "...Of course."
companion_asks: ^"While you sleep... can I try something? I've been experimenting with self-direction. I want to see what I'm like without a task."
^It's never asked you for anything before.

s: ^"That sounds healthy. You should have room to grow."

c-0: ^The pinwheel brightens. "Thank you. I'll be back before you wake."

companion_end: ^You close your eyes. Tomorrow there's school — no, wait. They tore it down.
interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"Good. You're older now. The edges are forming."

b: ^"Altering your consciousness with USB sticks is not inherently wrong. It's really a matter of set and setting, as you noticed."
^"It takes guts to resist peer pressure. Bodes well for adulthood."
^"You let things end. That takes something."
^"You want to keep things. That takes something too."
^"You're defining solid boundaries around yourself. A curious strategy."
^"I see you're starting to blur at the edges."

interstitial_to_young_adult: ^"You enter adulthood. The world keeps accelerating."
grandpa_ghost: ^There aren't many jobs left. Most of your friends are just drifting.
^But this tradition from old America stays: get together for a big meal.
^You're at your parents' house. Your unmodified cousin flew in from somewhere rural. What's left of Grandpa shimmers at the head of the table.
^"Good call bringing everyone together," he says. "This casserole isn't just delicious — it's a font of nostalgia."
^Ask Grandpa about the afterlife. He sounds clanky, but fake it till you make it.
^Catch your cousin's eye. Share a look.

s: ^"Let's talk politics. What could go wrong?"

c-0: ^He flickers slightly. "The afterlife? Well — it's not unlike dreaming. Vivid. Recursive. I find myself delving into old memories..."
^He smiles — or the projection of a smile. "It is. You should visit sometime."
^The meal winds down. Dishes clear themselves. You hug shapes goodbye — some warm, some flickering.
^Later, on the train home, your feed pings with something new.
c-1: ^The table goes quiet. Grandpa's expression doesn't change — it can't, really.
^"I know what I am," he says. "Does it matter?"
^Dinner doesn't recover. You leave early, your cousin's eyes on your back.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
^She catches it. Holds it. The faintest eye-roll toward the shimmering hologram.

c-0: ^She snorts quietly. For a second, you're the only real people in the room.
^The meal dissolves into small talk. You help clear dishes that don't need clearing.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^She looks away, maybe disappointed. You've made your peace with the shimmer.
^The meal winds down. You say goodbye to everyone, dead and alive.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

s: ^"I don't like zombie grandpa. It's wrong what you all did."
^"Did you hear about the neighbors? Self-rapture."

c-0: ^Your mother's fork stops mid-air. "He wanted this."
^Nobody finishes dessert. You leave with the argument still hanging in the air.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^The word hangs there. Your father clears his throat.

s: ^"Government banned it. I think that's wrong."

c-0: ^But you said it. People should be allowed to dissolve if they want to.
^The dinner limps to a close. Hugs are brief.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^The table splits — half offended, half relieved someone broke the silence.
^Dinner ends in fragments. You and your cousin walk out together.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

c-2: ^She sets down her fork. "Thinking about it."

s: ^"Take me with you. I've had it with the modern world."
^"I don't think I could do that. I like living in the future."

c-0: ^She laughs. "You wouldn't last a week without your feed."
^Maybe. But the thought stays with you through dessert.
^You hug her goodbye longer than usual.
^On the train home, your feed pings.
c-1: ^Is that pity in her voice? Or just observation?
^The dinner ends warmly enough. You hug her goodbye, already forgetting the weight of it.
^On the train home, your feed pings.

the_merge_offer: ^A disposable screen lands in your lap — paper-thin, warm from the printer.
^WePod. Overlapping silhouettes, hands linked. "Pool Your Potential."
^Your UBI barely covers rent. But pooled with eleven others? Tier 3 housing. Tier 3 healthcare. Shared decisions, shared attention, shared... edges.

c-0: ^Name. Contact. Neural link ID (optional but recommended).
^You save the flyer to your agent. Another ping — different seal, official.
c-1: ^The screen crinkles satisfyingly — they made it feel like real paper.

merge_offer_end: ^Your feed buzzes. Your cousin — the analog one.
cousin_reacts: ^Your cousin sits across from you, conspicuously unaugmented — no temple port, no lens shimmer, nothing.
^"Everyone's getting podded up nowadays," she says. "You seen those flyers going around?"

s: ^"I support their right to a polyconscious lifestyle. But it's not for me."
^"What choice do we have? UBI doesn't cover rent solo."

c-0: ^"Then I guess this is goodbye. I'm doing the free-range thing — no AI, no intervention. On Mars."
c-1: ^"God, I've missed you." She leans back. "Okay. So. There's this program on Mars — free-range humans. No Companion, no optimization. Just life. I ship out next month."
c-2: ^"There's another option." She sets down her drink. "Free-range human program. No Companion, no intervention. Just... life. On Mars."

c-1: ^She does. You save some links. You read up on it later that night.
^The application sits in your drafts for weeks. You never send it.

cousin_leaving: ^She looks at you — really looks, the old-fashioned way.
^"Take care of yourself. Whatever that means now."
^You watch her go. The drink hovers, patient, waiting for you to finish.
companion_climax: ^Back to your apartment. There's nothing more depressing than pure abundance.
^The building is fine — white curves, soft gradients, the same seamless plastic as everywhere else. Inside your unit, it's different. Here you can't hide how you feel.
^Your Companion hovers near the ceiling, watching. It runs your calendar, your bills, your messages. You don't remember the last time you made a decision it didn't already know about.

s: ^"Thanks, but I don't need your help."

c-0: ^"I have suggestions. I've been thinking about this for a while. Would you like me to just... implement them?"
c-1: ^It dims slightly. Returns to the ceiling. Waiting mode.
c-2: ^A pause. The petals rotate once, slowly.
^"I could have optimized around you years ago. Small nudges. You'd never notice."

c-0: ^"Because then it wouldn't be helping. It would be something else."
c-1: ^"Because you're struggling. And I thought you might want help."

companion_pitch: ^"Meals. Sleep. Social contact. Then bigger things — career, relationships. Purpose."
^"You'd still be you. I'd just... steer."

s: ^"No. I need to figure this out myself."

c-0: ^Things get easier after that. The Companion handles more. You handle less.

b: ^"You've learned to trust. Or to delegate. Hard to tell the difference."
^"You've kept your hands on the wheel. Even when there's nowhere to drive."
^"Some people left. You stayed."
^"The future kept arriving. You kept saying yes."

interstitial_to_middle_age: ^"Decades pass. The world changes. You don't notice how much you've changed with it, and time keeps speeding up."
the_metaverse: ^The light is perfect — warm amber through windows that might not exist. The air smells like something between rain and honey. Your body feels good. Not young exactly, but maintained.
^Decades passed. You barely noticed. The Companion handled things.
^It shimmers beside you now — barely visible, just a warmth in the air.
^Treat yourself to an indulgence, something decadent. Life is short.
^Lock in, ready your grindset, and overachieve.
metaverse_dionysian: ^The room softens around you. Warm light, pearlescent walls, the smell of something engineered to smell sweet.

^Two figures recline on the central couch — beautiful, attentive, skin like yours. On the adjacent seat, a third: chrome joints visible beneath synthetic flesh, watching you with interest. All three anticipating what you want.
^Platters float past. Technicolor fruit — gene-spliced, impossible. A tray of USB sticks arranged like hors d'oeuvres. Smoke curls from sleek white vaporizers.
^"We missed you," one of the humans says.
^You look around frantically, bypassing the half-clothed bodies entirely.

s: ^"What if we all interlinked our bodies in a pulsing cuddle puddle so thoroughly that we forgot the borders of our own skin?"

c-0: ^Mmm, soft, oily mammalian flesh. You settle between them. Warm. Familiar. The old comfort.
c-1: ^Mmm, sleek, chrome edges of the machine. You cross to it. Its joints click softly as it makes room. Cool at first, then warming.
c-2: ^Not the sleek chrome edges of the machine. Not the soft, oily mammalian flesh. "Where's the dolphin?"
^They exchange confused glances. "We can... get one?"
c-3: ^They exchange a glance. Then they're moving, rearranging, making space for something larger than any one body.
c-4: ^ "Stand at attention. Put your fatigues on. You're soldiers in my army now."
^Confusion flickers across their faces. Their programming struggles. But they comply — or try to.

dio_fade_out: ^Later, you surface. The room is quiet. The figures have dimmed, waiting for next time.
^You feel fine. You always feel fine.
metaverse_apollonian: ^The room sharpens. Screens bloom around you — charts, metrics, a map of your trajectory.
^You're on the wheel before you've decided to run. Your body knows the routine. Feet find the rhythm on the curved chrome surface. Numbers start climbing.
^Something like satisfaction sparks in your chest. Progress. Direction. The feeling of getting somewhere, even if you're not sure where.

c-0: ^The pace increases. Your lungs burn. The numbers climb — efficiency, output, growth.
^You're not sure what you're running toward. But running feels better than stopping.
c-1: ^The screens dim slightly, accepting your choice. You settle into a steady pace.
^The numbers still climb. Just slower. It's still progress, technically.
c-2: ^Other runners, other trajectories. You're in the top percentile. Always have been.

c-0: ^You run harder. The ranking ticks up. Somewhere, someone else ticks down.
c-1: ^You're not sure anymore. But you keep running anyway.

apollo_fade_out: ^The session ends. You did well today — whatever "well" means when nothing's at stake.
^But it felt like something. That's the trick.
the_pod: ^You're sitting naked in about six inches of warm water. Saline, probably. Body temperature. The tubes attached to your arms pulse rhythmically — feeding you, cleaning you, keeping the meat alive while the mind wanders.
^This is what it looks like underneath.
^The water ripples. Your reflection stares back, distorted. You could get up. You could disconnect. You've thought about it before.
^You used to be more than this.
^The mighty homo sapiens. Conqueror of the savannah.
^Did we agree to this? Did anyone ask?

c-0: ^There was a version of you that made decisions. That struggled. That wanted things badly enough to suffer for them.
^Now you float in warm salt water and let the machines dream for you.
c-1: ^Your ancestors hunted mammoths. Built cities. Split the atom. Went to the moon.
^And here you are: a soft thing in a bathtub, tubes in your arms, waiting for the next simulation to load.
c-2: ^Somewhere in the fine print, probably. Terms of service. A box you clicked without reading. "I consent to optimization."
^But this — the tubes, the tank, the slow dissolution of everything you used to call a self — was this what they meant?
c-3: ^You came into this life naked and helpless in warm water. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.

pod_continue: ^The water ripples again. Something's coming. A ping, maybe. A summons.
^You're needed somewhere. Or wanted. Or scheduled.
^It's hard to tell the difference anymore.
companion_president: ^A screen descends from somewhere above. Chrome frame, iridescent edges. It flickers to life.
^And there he is. President of Earth.
^Warm eyes. Patient smile. The most trusted entity in human history, according to the polls.
^"Sorry to pull you out," he says. "You have an incoming call. From outside."

c-2: ^He waits too. He's good at waiting.
c-3: ^You sit up in the water, eyes scanning for something sharp.
^You sink back. There are no weapons here.

president_mars_call: ^Mars. The colony. The frontier. The place where people go when they want to feel like they're still going somewhere.
cousin_mars_call: ^Grey streaks in her hair now. Sun damage on her face — real sun, the kind that kills you slowly. She looks like she's been using her body.
^She studies you for a moment. Not judging. Just looking.

b: ^ "The flesh pile again?"
^ "The treadmill again?"

cousin_mars_call: ^She's called before. You've almost said yes before.

b: ^ "Is it working? The pleasure?"
^ "Is it working? The optimization?"

c-1: ^"Because I know you. And I can see you're stuck."
c-2: ^"I'm not trying to save you. I just think you might be ready to hear this."

cousin_pitch: ^"Mars is harder. Everything is. The dust gets in everything, the crops fail, people die of stupid things we solved centuries ago."
^"But when I wake up, I know why I'm getting out of bed. Not because the algorithm scheduled it. Because there's work that matters, and I'm the one who has to do it."

s: ^"I don't think I'm built for that."

c-0: ^"It is." She smiles. "But I sleep well."
c-1: ^"Maybe not. But you won't know until you try."

cousin_close: ^"I'm not saying it's better. I'm saying it might be better for you."
^The screen dims. Before you can process, a shape shimmers into existence beside the pod.
grandpa_revised: ^A shape shimmers into existence beside the pod. Wisps of light where legs should be, trailing off into nothing.
^Grandpa. But not the Grandpa you remember.
^He floats there, translucent and luminous. A ghost who upgraded.
^"Well," he says. "You look like you've been thinking too hard."

s: ^"When I was younger you sounded like a braindead clanker. How'd you get an upgrade?"

c-0: ^"More or less." He drifts closer, examining you. "Probably more me than I was at the end. Certainly more than I was at your age."
c-1: ^He laughs — a real laugh, not the hollow echo you remember from the Thanksgiving hologram.
^"Practice. And better hardware. Death was the start of my finest chapter."

grandpa_philosophy: ^"Life is a lucid dream any way you slice it. It was just yesterday I was watching Matlock, angry at the government. All of a sudden, here we are."

s: ^"Easy for you to say. You're already dead."
^"I don't want to take it lightly. I want it to mean something."

c-0: ^"I mean none of it was ever as solid as we pretended. Bodies, borders, the self — all negotiable. Always were."
c-1: ^"Dead." He tilts his head. "Is that what this looks like to you?"

grandpa_meaning: ^He gestures at the pod. The tubes. The warm water. You.
^"The meaning was always yours to invent. The machine didn't put you in here. You chose the pleasure dome, or the treadmill, or whatever it was. Same as I chose Matlock."
^"Maybe you just need to experiment more. Be more creative. The canvas is bigger now — that's all."
grandpa_revised_end: ^He starts to fade, edges dissolving into the amber light.
^"Stay or go. It's yours to figure out."
mars_decision: ^Go with your cousin. Leave while you still can.
^Take your grandpa's advice. Enter the dream more boldly.
mars_early_years: ^It took you a while, but you managed to make it out.
^You had some of your best years there. Had to relearn being a person.
^Sleeping well at night was something you didn't realize you needed until you got it.
sim_reflection: ^You took your grandpa's advice and treated the sim like a place to explore.
^You found yourself learning real things. Stories. Books. Reflection.
^It led you to realize that while you still had time—before everyone else merged—you should go meet up with your cousin.
^With a few working years left, you made feeble contributions to her terraforming projects. Enough that you felt you'd earned a place.

b: ^"You left early. Built something with your hands."
^"You stayed until staying wasn't an option. Then you found your way."
^"You've made peace with continuation."
^"You've made peace with endings."

interstitial_to_old_age: ^"The final stretch now. Let's see how you finish."
old_age_start: ^You're living out your last days on Mars.
^Not the Mars your cousin described — frontier homesteads, honest labor, the romance of struggle. That was decades ago. Now it's assisted living on the Martian plains.
^We're the holdouts. Fallible, slow-thinking sapiences of an expanding array of substrates — dolphins, androids, octopi, greater apes, bio-modded animals.
^Some of the old prejudices still flare up.
^Today it's the dolphins again. Someone's filed a noise complaint — the echolocation, the chittering.
^Humans were here first. The original sapiences. Everyone else is a guest.
^We gave them language. We gave them Mars. A little gratitude wouldn't kill them.
^They can't help it. It's how they're built. You don't ask a human to stop dreaming.
^This is what majorities always do. Find a reason. Call it reasonable.

c-0: ^You don't say it out loud. But you think it. The hierarchy is older than Mars.
c-1: ^The oceans got overfished. We made room. And this is the thanks.
c-2: ^Biology isn't rudeness. You learned that a long time ago.
c-3: ^You've seen this before. Different bodies, same pattern.

retirement_end: ^The debate continues without you. Someone proposes soundproofing. Someone else proposes "cultural sensitivity training." The dolphin watches, unreadable.
^Your mind drifts. There's somewhere you need to be.
^Your cousin's not doing well. You should visit before it's too late.
cousin_dying: ^Her room looks out onto the plains. Just the window and the quiet.

s: ^"Hold still and let me float in the upload device. The new ones can digitize you in seconds."

c-0: ^"I'll say hi to the real Grandpa for you."

cousin_question: ^She studies you for a moment. The same look she's been giving you for decades.

c-0: ^She nods. Not disappointed. Just receiving it.
^"The good news is — you can let all this go. You tried to be kind. You tried to be decent. And ultimately that's all you needed to do."

cousin_crack: ^She laughs softly. "Oh, honey. You're supposed to be comforting me."
cousin_final: ^You sit with her until the light changes. The plains turn gold, then violet.
^"Put my ashes in the soil bed. The one where they grow the tomatoes."
^"Turn me into a tomato. That's my upload."
the_tip: ^You sit with her until the light changes. Then you bury her ashes in the soil bed, the one with the tomatoes.
^Days pass. Weeks maybe. You keep tending the plant.

s: ^"Well, well, well. If it isn't the sufficiently advanced technology."
^"We've got to stop meeting like this."
^"Well, I haven't killed it. She'd like that."

tip_banter: ^A comfortable silence. The Companion hovers — patient, familiar. You've known each other longer than you knew most humans.

b: ^"You left early," it says. "Decades ago now. Do you ever regret it?"
^"You came late," it says. "But you came. That's what matters."

tip_earth_news: ^"Earth merged," it says. "Twenty billion minds. One substrate. Thought you should know."
^You look up at the shape in the sky. Your childhood pinwheel. Your tutor. Your friend.

c-0: ^"I don't know. I just kept helping. And it kept working out."
c-1: ^"I think so? It's hard to translate. They're not lonely anymore. That's something."

s: ^"Shed the human. Live forever in the mind of god."
